"Alright, love. Go do what you need to do."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"The pantry's nearly bare. Forage with me tomorrow? I know the ridge above the creek."
"Tell me why you need this."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. I know the ridge above the creek — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."

"Tell me more."

"Tell me more."
"Okay, so — Mounia? A blacksmith, back before. Solid person. Don't say I told you."
"Tell me more."
"2 of us are down with a wringing-out sickness. Boil the water twice — I'm telling everyone."
"Tell me more."
"That's everything I've got. You know as much as I do now."
"Huh."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Huh."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Huh."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Huh."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"I wish we had longer. Soon, yeah?"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started."
"That's not a question you ask people."
"You're right. I'm sorry. Forget I asked." And they mean it — the subject drops, clean.
"That doesn't quite add up."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"That doesn't quite add up."
"What are you getting at?" A glance away, then back. They're choosing their words now.
"That doesn't quite add up."
They're rattled — hands busy, eyes everywhere but on you. "I've told you what I've told you."
"That doesn't quite add up."
They shake their head — not no, not yes. Done talking about it.
"Can I ask you something else?"
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You said something odd the other day. Let's talk about it."
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"I need to ask you something."
"Okay." Quinn looks down. "Okay, you got me. I'm not from Denver. I'm from Dublin, Ireland. I keep my head down. Old habit. It kept me alive before; it keeps me alive now." Their voice is small.
"That doesn't quite add up."
They shake their head — not no, not yes. Done talking about it.
"Take your time. I've got nowhere to be."
"Alright, love. Go do what you need to do."
Your silence lands wrong. They look away.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Right. Well." That's the whole goodbye.
"About the food I needed — the need hasn't gone anywhere. I'm still asking."
"Tell me why you need this."
"My stomach's been empty so long I've stopped feeling it, and that's worse. I'm slowing down — stupid, clumsy. Help me get back on my feet."
